original_test_intent: Verify the complete SMBIOS Type 11 OEM Strings structure, including Count and every OEM string, matches the approved system recipe and remains identical after a controlled reboot.
original_method: On the same verified SUT, preserve baseline logs, capture complete raw and decoded Type 11 data, compare structure count and protected string identities to the approved recipe, perform an authorized reboot, repeat collection and compare persistence.
manual_activity: The owner supplies the expected Type 11 content/redaction policy and approves the reboot; an operator supervises workload safety and recovery. Collection/comparison can then be automated.
required_inputs: Exact SUT, hardware recipe, BIOS/SMBIOS and dmidecode identities
Expected Type 11 structure count plus per-record OEM string inventory or approved hashed patterns
Multiple-record, empty-string, duplicate, ordering and encoding rules
Sensitive/customer/provisioning string protection and evidence access policy
Approved reboot method, workload window, boot deadline and independent console recovery
Secure access and complete raw SMBIOS parsing tooling
safety_requirements: Do not clear dmesg, syslog or SEL; preserve pre-existing evidence
Keep collection read-only and never modify SMBIOS, BIOS or recipe state
Use protected credentials and verified host identity; reject StrictHostKeyChecking=no patterns
Redact or hash sensitive OEM strings only under the approved policy while retaining controlled raw evidence
Require approval before reboot and stop on failed recovery, wrong target or unexpected content drift
Do not automatically rerun a reboot or collection after an ambiguous failure
agent_execution_scope: Verify same-target identity and approved recipe/redaction/reboot inputs
Collect complete raw Type 11 output and parse every record/count/string boundary
Perform only the approved reboot after user confirmation
Compare pre/post structure, values and protected identities and preserve logs
Make no firmware change, secret disclosure, automatic retry or PASS/FAIL verdict
engineer_actions: Approve expected OEM-string matrix, multiple-record semantics and redaction policy
Approve workload-safe reboot and recovery plan
Review any count/value/persistence anomaly and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `dmidecode -t 11` is relevant, but the insecure SSH wrapper and `grep -A1` neither preserve the full record nor execute the required reboot persistence comparison.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Securely capture complete `dmidecode -t 11` stdout/stderr and exit status before and after one approved reboot, parse all record boundaries and compare protected count/value identities.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Type 11 OEM Strings, Count, recipe correctness, before/after reboot persistence, source script and 5/5-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: PACKAGE-GATED COMPLETE TYPE 11 PRE/POST REBOOT VALIDATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Hash the complete raw captures, parse declared count and each record-local string through the terminator, apply controlled redaction and compare both expected recipe and pre/post persistence on the same SUT.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Rejects destructive log clearing and insecure filtered transport while implementing the source's full Count and reboot-persistence scope.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A header plus one following line can miss additional strings, multiple structures, malformed termination and changes after reboot; complete record-aware evidence closes those gaps.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OEM strings are vendor-defined and may include sensitive identifiers. Technical parsing cannot determine semantic correctness without the owner-approved recipe and protection policy.

project_override_considerations: A project-specific allowed string change must be versioned against exact BIOS/recipe identity and visible in the comparison; it cannot waive internal count/string consistency or evidence protection.
expected_evidence: Verified SUT/recipe/BIOS/SMBIOS/dmidecode identity and approved Type 11 matrix
Complete protected raw/decoded Type 11 before reboot with per-record declared/enumerated counts
Approved reboot/boot timeline and same-target proof
Complete protected post-reboot capture and expected/pre/post value, count, ordering and encoding diff
Preserved baseline/post logs, no-clear/no-write/no-auto-retry audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria coherently require Type 11 Count/content correctness and persistence after reboot. The insecure filtered DeepSeek command is an incomplete implementation, not a competing source requirement.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The expected OEM-string matrix and reboot approval are normal package/user inputs; they gate execution but do not prevent independent static review.

review_improvement: Preserves the full Type 11 and reboot scope while replacing a filtered one-shot command and destructive log clearing with secure complete record-aware comparison.
independent_technical_reasoning: SMBIOS Type 11 correctness has two separable invariants: each record's declared Count must match its local string set, and the owner-approved string identities must persist across reboot. A filtered `grep -A1` cannot establish either invariant when multiple strings or structures exist. Because strings may contain provisioning data, comparisons need controlled raw custody plus redacted or hashed reporting rather than dropping content entirely.
